title: Permutation isomorphism preserves coefficient sections
statement: For schemes X,S, m ≥ 0, morphisms pr_i : X → P¹_S indexed by Fin(m+1), an endomorphism f : X → X and a permutation π with f followed by pr_i = pr_π(i), let L and F_j be the ordered tensor line bundle and coefficient sections [def-weil-pbc-symmetric-product-sections]. There exists an isomorphism β : f^* L ≅ L [def-pc-module-pullback], carrying the adjunction-unit pullback [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction] of each F_j to F_j. No inverse of f or product universal property is required.

proof.text: For a list of factor indices, form the right-associated tensor product ending in the unit and its pure tensor section. Induction on List.Perm constructs a section-preserving isomorphism: identity for nil; tensor with identity for cons; inverse associator, braiding, then associator for an adjacent swap; composition for transitivity. The structural maps act on tensor sections by their explicit section formulas.

Compare the left-associated positive tensor with the right-associated list tensor. A snoc comparison follows by induction on the list using unitors and associators. Induction on m then gives the comparison for List.ofFn. Apply the list permutation theorem to the enumeration π and compose the comparisons. This isomorphism sends a permuted family of pure section tensors to its original order.

Pullback commutes with positive tensor products, with pure-section compatibility, by induction on m and module_pullback_tensor. In each factor the composition comparison identifies f^*(pr_i^*O(1)) with (f followed by pr_i)^*O(1). Rewrite the latter map using the given equality with pr_π(i). Compatibility with adjunction units identifies both pulled coordinate sections. Tensor these factor isomorphisms and compose with the permutation comparison of the previous step.

The resulting β sends the pure term indexed by J to the term indexed by π(J). Pullback and β are additive. Reindex the finite sum defining F_j along the equivalence J ↦ J.map π.toEmbedding, which preserves cardinality. Hence β takes every pulled coefficient section back to itself.

lean.statement:
theorem symmetricProduct_sections_permutation {S X : Scheme.{v}} (m : ℕ)
    (pr : Fin (m + 1) → (X ⟶ ℙ(ULift.{v} (Fin 2); S)))
    (f : X ⟶ X) (π : Equiv.Perm (Fin (m + 1)))
    (hf : ∀ i, f ≫ pr i = pr (π i)) :
    ∃ β : (Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback f).obj (symmetricProductLineBundle pr) ≅
        symmetricProductLineBundle pr,
      ∀ j : ULift.{v} (Fin (m + 2)),
        β.hom.app ⊤ (((Classical.choose
          (Scheme.Modules.exists_tensorPullbackAdjunction f)).unit.app
            (symmetricProductLineBundle pr)).val.app (Opposite.op ⊤)
              ((symmetricProductCoordinateSection pr j).val (Opposite.op ⊤))) =
          (symmetricProductCoordinateSection pr j).val (Opposite.op ⊤)
